tagline: Up the Potomac from Mount Vernon, on the old trolley bed.
intro: The parkway starts at a traffic circle by Mount Vernon and heads north up the Virginia bank of the Potomac, at first on the right-of-way of the old trolley line to Alexandria, with the Mount Vernon Trail running alongside. Through Old Town it becomes Washington Street. North of town it takes up the river again, past the airport and Roosevelt Island, with rest areas looking across to the Georgetown skyline and the Potomac Palisades, and ends at the Beltway near McLean.

The first stretch opened in January 1932 for Washington's 200th birthday, with President Hoover driving at the head of twelve cars. Short of lights and still unfinished, it opened only on weekends, by daylight, until March.

moments.title: Dyke Marsh
moments.text: Fresh water from the upper Potomac floats over the salt tide here, and the old Haul Road leads birdwatchers out into the marsh from the Belle Haven Marina exit.

moments.title: Jones Point Light
moments.text: A one-story lighthouse of 1855, dark now, with the south cornerstone of the 1791 District of Columbia boundary survey still set in the seawall beside it.

moments.title: Theodore Roosevelt Island
moments.text: No cars cross. A footbridge from the Arlington bank leads into a forest that 1930s landscape architects designed to imitate the one that once covered the island.

practical: Trucks and other commercial vehicles are prohibited on the parkway, though taxis and airport shuttles may use it.
